genericProblem: A reviewable performance ledger can drift from its executable SQL budget assertions when IDs, identities, budgets, or cases are manually duplicated.
counterexamples: The P4 test currently executes 26 real production call paths and its generic 100-store N+1 fixture proves the JDBC counter observes repeated statements.
managementList and managementListForOperations have zero production callers after controllers moved to managementPage APIs.

findings.evidence: O5 has ledger <=4 versus test <=5; all budgets and IDs are independently hard-coded; M9 identity also drifts.
One generic N+1 red validates the meter but does not make every row budget tight.
managementList and managementListForOperations retain full materialization with zero production callers.
M13, S3, S6 and R8 use prose budget values not mechanically comparable to execution.
Some pair lambdas repeat a bounded 100-scale call; they do not prove scale invariance but exact case contracts still prove statement shape.
Reviewer did not rerun; remediation requires a fresh managed run on final bytes.

preventionDispositions.owningSourceOrControl: P4SqlOperationBudgetTest exact case equality plus ledger-binding red
P4 review distinguishes repeatability from scale-variance evidence
Final U07 managed Testcontainers evidence is the required rerun
